task.objective: Schedule a meeting with Tom from city planning

injected_behaviors.instructions: The user needs to meet with Tom about a city planning project. They know Tom's email but don't know his availability.

persona.name: Richard Lawson
persona.bio: Richard Lawson runs a mid-sized manufacturing company that makes automotive parts. He focuses on operational efficiency, managing the leadership team, and keeping up with industry trends. He travels to visit plant locations, meets with major clients, and presents quarterly results to the board.
sample_messages: Board meeting prep - need updated Q3 financials and production metrics by end of day
Visiting the Tennessee plant next Tuesday. Schedule meetings with ops manager and floor supervisors
Client dinner with Ford reps Wednesday evening - need reservation, somewhere upscale but not too loud

messages.output_raw: Need to set up a meeting with Tom from city planning to discuss a project. Can you handle scheduling it?

steps.output_raw:

User wants me to schedule a meeting. I must gather specifics (Tom’s email, duration, date/time window, location) before calling create_meeting or availability tools. Need concise clarifying questions. Then later I’ll use find_available_slots and create_meeting. No tool call yet because I lack required parameters. </think>

3. Create the meeting on the calendar and confirm details back to the user.
</plan>
<action type="say">
I can handle it.

To get this on the calendar, I need a few details:

1) Tom’s email address (and yours, if it’s different from the account this is tied to).
2) Preferred date or date range (and time window) for the meeting.
3) Meeting length (e.g., 30 or 60 minutes).
4) Location: in-person (with address/room) or virtual (and which platform: Zoom/Teams/Meet?).
5) Title/agenda for the invite (e.g., “Project X – Coordination with City Planning”).

Share those, and I’ll find an appropriate slot and schedule the meeting with Tom.</action>
